name: Pancreatic Divisum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Imaging-based Diagnostic Criteria for Pancreatic Divisum

criteria.description: Failure of dorsal and ventral pancreatic ducts to fuse on imaging
Presence of a dominant dorsal pancreatic duct draining the majority of the pancreas
Pancreatic secretions predominantly draining through the minor papilla
Lack of communication between ventral and dorsal ducts on MRCP or ERCP

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of non-fusion of pancreatic ducts with dominant dorsal duct drainage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as MRCP or ERCP.

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes of pancreatitis without other identifiable causes

searchTerms: feeling sick along with belly pain
throwing up with acute pancreatic inflammation
nausea and vomiting in pancreatitis flare-ups

common.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic pain or malabsorption
searchTerms: weight loss from chronic pain or digestion issues
losing weight due to ongoing abdominal pain
weight decline related to malabsorption or pain

common.symptomName: Steatorrhea secondary to exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
searchTerms: fatty stools from poor pancreatic enzyme function
oily, foul-smelling stools due to digestion problems

occasional.symptomName: Jaundice due to pancreatic duct obstruction
searchTerms: yellowing of skin from blocked pancreatic duct
jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellow discoloration from pancreatic blockage

occasional.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to endocrine insufficiency
searchTerms: secondary diabetes due to endocrine issues
high blood sugar from gland failure
increased fluid pressure inside pancreatic ducts
death of pancreatic tissue in severe inflammation
tissue damage in pancreas from inflammation

rare.symptomName: Splenic vein thrombosis secondary to inflammation
searchTerms: blood clot in splenic vein due to inflammation
splenic vein thrombosis secondary to pancreatic disease
vein blockage near spleen caused by inflammation

laboratory: Elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute pancreatitis episodes
Possible impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes markers
imaging: MRCP showing non-fusion of dorsal and ventral pancreatic ducts
ERCP demonstrating dominant dorsal duct drainage through minor papilla
CT scan showing pancreatic inflammation or pseudocysts
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; congenital anomaly
other: Endoscopic ultrasound may assist in ductal anatomy visualization
Secretin stimulation test may show impaired drainage

distinguishingFeatures: History of alcohol use or other etiologies
Weight loss without recurrent pancreatitis episodes

redFlags: Signs of pancreatic necrosis or infection
New onset diabetes mellitus in young patient with pancreatitis
